comment: lex_token contracts WITH + ROLLUP_SYM into one token
WITH + CUBE_SYM
WITH + SYSTEM
any other follower is buffered in lookahead_token and returned next
the lookahead at end of query is END_OF_INPUT, which the parser sees after WITH
the second lex_one_token call skips comments, so the contraction still fires; the merged token spans both lexemes
whitespace between the two words does not matter
FOR + SYSTEM_TIME_SYM -> FOR_SYSTEM_TIME_SYM
any other follower is buffered
VALUES + LESS_SYM (partition bounds)
VALUES + IN_SYM
with parsing_place == NO_MATTER (valid() false everywhere) the follower is buffered and VALUES is returned
VALUE_SYM is returned unchanged when no parsing_place applies
the buffered token is returned by the early `lookahead_token >= 0` branch, which is *before* the merge switch: a contraction is not applied to it
same, without a follower

parsing_place IN_UPDATE_ON_DUP_KEY/IN_PART_FUNC -> VALUE_SYM. valid(VALUE_SYM) and not valid(VALUES) is true here, but nothing in the shifted prefix can have run sql_yacc.yy:14485 or sql_yacc.yy:5151, so the C's parsing_place is NO_MATTER and the token stays VALUES
when both are acceptable the predicate is false and VALUES stays VALUES

parsing_place BEFORE_OPT_LIST/AFTER_LIST returns VALUES *without* the lookahead. Not armed here: no CREATE/INSERT/REPLACE was shifted, so sql_yacc.yy:2651/14243/14324 cannot have run and the C takes the lookahead and contracts
when VALUES_LESS_SYM is acceptable the contraction is what the parser wants

parsing_place BEFORE_OPT_LIST/AFTER_LIST turns VALUE_SYM into VALUES. Not armed here: with no CREATE/INSERT/REPLACE in the prefix the C's parsing_place is NO_MATTER, so `value (1)` stays VALUE_SYM - this is the `value(1,'two')` over-accept
both acceptable -> no swap

the armed twin of vld-values-to-value: after ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (sql_yacc.yy:14485) parsing_place is IN_UPDATE_ON_DUP_KEY, so VALUES becomes the VALUE_SYM function of sql_yacc.yy:10676 - while the insert's own VALUES, read before the flag was armed, is left alone
sql: INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (1) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE a=VALUES(b)

comment: IN_PART_FUNC (sql_yacc.yy:5151) is armed by LIST_SYM followed by the '(' of part_func and cleared at its ')' (sql_yacc.yy:5156), so the second `values` is outside the window
the sibling `LIST_SYM part_column_list` (sql_yacc.yy:5158) never sets IN_PART_FUNC; the follower COLUMNS tells the two apart, so `values` is not rewritten
a reserved word stays reserved where the C's flag cannot be set: `values` after CREATE PROCEDURE is not an sp name, which is why the server rejects CREATE PROCEDURE values()

the armed twin of vld-value-to-values: insert_start (sql_yacc.yy:14243) sets BEFORE_OPT_LIST, and the grammar has no VALUE_SYM spelling of the insert verb, so INSERT INTO t VALUE (1) only parses if the lexer swaps the token
the `create:` setter (sql_yacc.yy:2651) arms the same swap for CREATE TABLE ... VALUE (1)
the armed twin of vld-values-before-opt-list: with INSERT shifted, BEFORE_OPT_LIST is reachable and the C returns VALUES with no lookahead, so no contraction happens
parsing_place == BEFORE_OPT_LIST and the follower is neither '(' nor SELECT nor VALUES -> LEFT_PAREN_ALT (CREATE TABLE t (col ...))
CREATE TABLE t2 (LIKE t1)
CREATE TABLE t (WITH cte AS ...)
SELECT as the follower keeps the plain '('

VALUES as the follower keeps the plain '('. The fixture has no second '(' on purpose: valid() is a constant set here, while the C clears parsing_place to NO_MATTER after the first use, so a nested '(' would be gated differently by the two - that coupling is what `lexdump.py --valid replay` exists for
a '(' follower keeps the plain '(' - and the buffered '(' is returned from lookahead_token without going through the switch again
no LEFT_PAREN_* is acceptable, which stands for parsing_place != BEFORE_OPT_LIST -> plain '('
--valid all makes the gate true, which is what the 'all' mode documents
under --valid all both VALUES predicates are false (each is 'X and not Y'), so the contraction is what remains
the PARTITION_SYM/SELECT_SYM/UNION_SYM case only clears parsing_place; it never changes a token
same for PARTITION
same for UNION
